### Observed differences

- In the earlier window the sequence ran A20 → A30/A31/A36 → A22 → A21 → A25: A20's outgoing transitions led to A30 in about 40 in 100 cases, A31 in about 33 and A36 in about 28; each of the three then led to the other two group members and to A22 in roughly equal shares (about 28–39 in 100 each); A22 and then A21 followed (median positions about 0.47 and 0.63 of the trace), and A21 was followed by A25 one step later in all 200 traces. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG004, POS001, POS002]
- In the later window the group sits later in the sequence: A20 leads directly to A22 (about 99 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, one step apart instead of four), A21 now leads into the group (A30 about 36 in 100, A31 about 33, A36 about 31, with A25 chosen in only about 1 in 100), and the group members now exit to A25 (about 31–36 in 100) instead of to A22 (about 0.5 in 100). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001]
- The order between the group and A21/A22 reversed: earlier, each of A30, A31 and A36 ran before A21 and before A22 in 100 in 100 traces; later, A21 and A22 each run before them in about 99 in 100 traces, while the activities still co-occur in every trace in both windows. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- Event positions shifted consistently with this: the median position of A30, A31 and A36 moved from about 0.41 to about 0.59 of the trace, A21 from about 0.63 to 0.53, and A22 from about 0.47 to 0.37. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- Distances changed accordingly: A21 and A25 are now about four steps apart (previously adjacent), and the pairs A20–A31, A20–A36, A31–A22 and A36–A22 fall within five steps of each other in only about 2 of 200 later traces, against all 200 earlier traces; these four profiles rest on only about 2 later observations each. [LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]
- No participation difference underlies this: every activity involved occurs in essentially all traces in both windows (directional and positional support 200 of 200; co-occurrence 1.0), so the difference is one of order, not of activities appearing or disappearing. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the block of activities A30, A31 and A36 changed its placement in the sequence: it ran between A20 and A22 in the earlier window (A20 → A30/A31/A36 → A22 → A21 → A25) and, in the later window, runs after A21 (A20 → A22 → A21 → A30/A31/A36 → A25). A20 now bypasses the block and leads directly to A22, A21 now leads into the block, and the block leads to A25 instead of A22, while its internal, unfixed order is unchanged. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG004, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]

The change is shown directly and consistently: six relation items record the order reversal itself (100 in 100 one way earlier, about 99 in 100 the other way later, with co-occurrence unchanged), the successor changes at A20, A21 and all three block members match the same relocation, and the position and distance shifts agree in direction and size. In total 22 control-flow items qualified against roughly 0.42 expected for an unchanged process, and every item's difference exceeds about 199 of 200 random re-splits, so sampling alone cannot account for them. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]

The evidence cannot rule out that the two windows sample two different end-to-end variants whose shares flipped, rather than a single relocated block; the four lag profiles now resting on about 2 traces are individually weak, though they are corroborated by the directional and relation items. [LAG002, LAG003, LAG005, LAG006]
